subject.title: [Bug]: OpenAI-compatible streaming tool calls are dropped when provider omits finish_reason

question: Should OpenClaw treat native streamed `delta.tool_calls` plus a clean SSE `[DONE]` terminator as sufficient tool-use intent when an OpenAI-compatible provider omits `finish_reason`?
rationale: The source-level failure is clear, but the remaining choice is the provider-compatibility and tool-execution safety contract for no-finish streams.

options.title: Accept clean `[DONE]` as tool-use intent
options.body: Land a narrowly guarded fix like the open PR so native tool calls execute only when the stream terminates cleanly and has no visible-text ambiguity.

options.title: Keep `finish_reason` mandatory
options.body: Leave current behavior unchanged and document that OpenAI-compatible streaming providers must emit a tool-use or stop finish reason for executable tool calls.

options.title: Require an opt-in compatibility mode
options.body: Add a provider-level setting for no-finish tool-call promotion if maintainers want this behavior only for known-compatible routes.

recommendation.title: Accept clean `[DONE]` as tool-use intent
recommendation.body: Land a narrowly guarded fix like the open PR so native tool calls execute only when the stream terminates cleanly and has no visible-text ambiguity.

likelyOwner.reason: They reviewed and approved the adjacent finish-reason/tool-call execution contract changes and are the clearest owner for accepting or rejecting the widened contract.
